Formulation
Predisposing: Possible tendency toward health anxiety (no prior documentation).
Precipitating: Recent onset of left-sided hearing loss, facial numbness, ringing, dizziness.
Perpetuating: Internet searches amplifying worry; occupational impact reinforcing concern.
Protective: Supportive partner, willingness to seek medical care, functional employment.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s):
  • Understand the cause of physical symptoms and reduce panic.
  • Resume normal training/work without health worry.

- Clinical Goal(s):
  • Reduce health-related anxiety and catastrophic interpretations.
  • Provide accurate medical information and reassurance following physical assessment.

- Actions (Patient):
  • Attend same-day in-person GP appointment for neurological/ENT assessment.
  • Limit unverified online health searches; use trusted medical resources provided.
  • Monitor anxiety levels and note triggers.

- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  • Complete physical and neurological examination; clarify diagnosis (e.g., rule out Bell’s palsy).
  • Provide clear explanation of findings and expected course.
  • Offer brief psychoeducation on health anxiety and normal stress responses.
  • Consider referral to psychology or brief CBT for health anxiety if distress persists after physical issues addressed.
  • Document outcomes and update mental health plan accordingly.

Secondary Problem: Not recorded

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: No (pending in-person consultation). Topics to cover: Bell’s palsy/ear pathology basics; health-related anxiety; reliable information sources.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Escalating panic, excessive internet searching, further occupational impairment.
- Coping Strategies: Scheduled worry time, relaxation breathing, limit online searches, seek timely medical advice.

Consent, Coordination & Review
- Patient Consent to Plan: Not recorded
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: To be set after physical assessment (suggest 4–6 weeks)

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: Formal mental health diagnosis, detailed substance/alcohol history, sleep/appetite details, formal risk screening, documented consent.  
● Internal conflicts: Living situation initially “lives alone,” later “lives with partner” (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality notes: No DOB, contact details, or GP details provided; primary focus of consult was physical, with limited mental health content.
